denial.text: Lanternhill Health Plan denied the claim for CPT 19318 (bilateral reduction mammaplasty) with date of service 2026-06-16. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation submitted does not establish failure of conservative therapy or an expected resection weight meeting the policy threshold.

criteria.text: Symptoms attributable to macromastia documented for at least 12 months, such as neck, shoulder, or upper back pain, shoulder grooving, or inframammary intertrigo.
At least 6 months of conservative treatment, including a supportive garment plus physical therapy, analgesics, or dermatologic treatment of intertrigo, without adequate relief.
Estimated resection of at least 500 grams per breast.
Photographic documentation of macromastia and shoulder grooving.

chart.text: From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

34 year old woman here about her breasts, referred by her primary. Exam: large pendulous breasts, nipple to notch 33 on the right and 34 on the left, grade 3 ptosis, intertrigo in both inframammary folds. Discussed reduction, risks, scars, sensation, the works. Her history otherwise: seasonal allergies. Surgeries: wisdom teeth. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Quit smoking 13 years ago, no alcohol, drives for a living. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. She has had the neck and upper back pain for 16 months now, maybe longer, says it is daily by the afternoon. The bra straps have worn grooves into both shoulders and she gets the rash under the breasts every summer. She has been in a fitted supportive bra from the specialty shop for months, takes ibuprofen most days, treats the rash with nystatin powder. I am sending her to PT for posture and scapular work. She is 5 foot 4, 218 pounds, which puts BSA right around 2.11. Schnur 22nd percentile at that BSA is about 769 grams. I am estimating 627 grams on the right and 615 on the left.
Eval for upper back and neck pain in the setting of large breasts. Forward shoulder posture, tight pecs, weak lower traps. Plan 12 weeks, twice a week, scapular stabilization and postural retraining.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Session 2. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.
Session 3. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.
Session 4. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.
Session 5. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.

Back to go over the plan. Symptoms unchanged. We went through the operation again and she wants to proceed if insurance will cover it. Vitals today 124 over 74, pulse 66. Finished 12 weeks of PT across the street, says it helped while she was there and then right back to baseline. Still in the supportive bra, still on the ibuprofen, intertrigo treated with nystatin powder with partial relief. That is 7 months of conservative measures without durable relief.
Standard pre-op photo series taken today, front, both obliques, both laterals. Grooving visible at both shoulders in the AP view, grade 3 ptosis, intertrigo in both folds.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 18 and 15. No ocular pathology noted.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Blood pressure check. 127 over 86 today, 144 over 84 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 8 weeks.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
She called asking where things stand with the insurance. Told her the paperwork went in and we are waiting to hear. Reviewed what to do in the meantime.
Patient called about a tick bite on the calf after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 216, LDL 153, HDL 41, triglycerides 119. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Vitamin D came back 20. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
A1c came back 6.8. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Interval visit. Nothing new since last time, symptoms as described before, she is managing. Went over the plan again and answered questions from her spouse.

Here with a cough and congestion for 8 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 4 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Pre-op visit. Consent signed, marked the plan on her in the mirror, superomedial pedicle, Wise pattern. Labs fine. Stop the ibuprofen a week out.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
